name: LTX-2.3 Identity (TalkVid 3k)
means: Holds one person's face steady across a video clip. Trained on talking-head footage, so the case it is built for is a character speaking to camera.
verdict: IT LOADS AND RUNS, AND IT DOES NOTHING MEASURABLE IN THE CONFIGURATION THIS REPO CAN USE. Wired as epic.py wires an id_lora - a second LoraLoaderModelOnly chained after the distill LoRA, model into CFGGuider - and rendered at 0.0 (node absent), 0.5 and 1.0 on two keyframes with faces. Scored on a FACE CROP, not the whole frame, because a face is ~14% of the pixels and a melting face barely moves a global SSIM. Face SSIM of the final frame vs the keyframe: kfB 0.2485 off / 0.2478 at 0.5 / 0.2465 at 1.0; kfA 0.1932 / 0.1879 / 0.2033. The spread across those three is smaller than the spread the SAME config shows across seeds (kfA face SSIM ranges 0.168-0.218 over 4 seeds), so this is indistinguishable from noise. The frame strips at 1.0 and at off are not tellable apart by eye. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON WHAT WAS NOT TESTED: ComfyUI's video_ltx2_3_id_lora.json template does not use this LoRA as a bare model patch. It routes the model through LTXVReferenceAudio with a driving reference_audio, plus a two-stage LTXVLatentUpsampler pipeline. This file is trained on talking-head footage and its intended input is a voice track. The verdict is therefore 'no effect as a drop-in for short.py', NOT 'the LoRA does not work'. Testing it properly means building the reference-audio graph. Evidence: studio/samples/video_engines/.
note: base_model INFERRED, and note the distinction from the two LTX files that state a version: this file's __metadata__ key is PRESENT BUT EMPTY - zero keys - which is a different thing from absent and worth recording, because an empty dict means the training rig wrote metadata support and then wrote nothing into it. The inference rests on 48 transformer_blocks plus the audio_attn1 / audio_attn2 / video_to_audio_attn / audio_ff families, which match the two files that DO say 2.3.0, plus the filename. That is structural evidence, not a version read: it could be another LTX-2.x revision. | purpose is name-inferred. 'id-lora' and 'talkvid' are strong hints and nothing more; no file in this set states its purpose. | WHY IT MATTERS HERE: identity across a clip is a problem this project has not solved on the video side at all. On the anime path a character is held by a trained LoRA plus IPAdapter; on qwen by a reference sheet; on VIDEO by nothing - the keyframe is conditioned and then the video model is left to its own devices. If this works it is the missing third mechanism. | NOT WIRED into any studio workflow. trigger unknown. 1728 tensors, rank 128, no alpha so scale 1.0. Everything on this card except the geometry is a guess, which is why status is untested and strength is a convention rather than a measurement.
